subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What permanent contract should `clawhub skill publish` use for publisher-declared GitHub source metadata?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current trusted/untrusted separation but cannot determine whether maintainers want to expose unverified attribution, deprecate the flags, or fund server-side verification; each choice changes the public contract and security boundary.

options.title: Add two-tier attribution
options.body: Preserve and expose publisher-declared source as explicitly unverified metadata while reserving verification and trust indicators for server-resolved provenance.

options.title: Document or deprecate flags
options.body: Keep direct skill publishes without visible source attribution and clearly document, warn on, or remove flags that currently imply a stronger result.

options.title: Build verified publishing
options.body: Verify repository identity, commit, path, and uploaded content server-side before recording CLI-published source as trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Add two-tier attribution
recommendation.body: Preserve and expose publisher-declared source as explicitly unverified metadata while reserving verification and trust indicators for server-resolved provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent GitHub-backed source-sync work provides the strongest available context for choosing and implementing the provenance contract.
